html:
SMTO-ART-0006 — This file belongs to a different conversation

GUID: b7a5a040-e3f1-499c-826c-5885c6221ec6
Slug: artifact-wrong-scope
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO only opens a Task's saved files from the conversation where that Task ran. This file is tied to another conversation, or its files were deleted, so SMTO didn't open it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Go to the conversation where the Task ran. If this conversation was started with Continue in new conversation, select View source in its 'Continued from previous conversation' card. Only the original conversation can open all of that Task's files and use Retry collection.
  2. In that conversation, open Artifacts from this run for the Task and select the file from that list. The list always opens files through the conversation they belong to, so SMTO can confirm access.
  3. If the list says the files from this run have been deleted, ask SMTO in a new message to create the file again. Deleted Task files can't be reopened, but running the request again makes a fresh copy.

What success looks like

  • The file opens or downloads from the Artifacts list in the conversation where its Task ran.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, saying which conversation you were in. Don't copy the file into another Task's folder by hand to make it show up here.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Artifact authorization rejected the request because the run's workspace belongs to another conversation without a grant, is retired or deleted, or the Gateway's temp mapping directories do not match the run's workspace.

What this means

  • Artifact authorization finds wrong/missing conversation/run ownership or grant, deleted/retired scope, or temporary environment directories inconsistent with the expected run scope. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Artifact authorization finds wrong/missing conversation/run ownership or grant, deleted/retired scope, or temporary environment directories inconsistent with the expected run scope.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare exact scope identities, retained grants and managed directory mapping.

How to fix it

  • Compare the request's conversation_id with artifact_workspaces.conversation_id for the run and check artifact_grants (forked conversations get read grants but cannot call the artifacts reconcile endpoint). A retired workspace or a Gateway .retired fence means the files were deleted; for the temp-mapping variant, compare OF_RUN_TEMP_DIR, OF_RUN_ARTIFACT_DIR and OF_RUN_SCRATCH_DIR with the layout under the Gateway's GATEWAY_ARTIFACT_ROOT.
  • Open the owning conversation and run or select an artifact within the current scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The operation uses the intended authorized scope without substituting another run's paths.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
